meta_description: Hundreds of agents as one governed fleet — roles, queues, budgets and audit for the AI workforce.

blocks.x: Hundreds of agents as one governed fleet — roles, queues, budgets and audit for the AI workforce.

Scaling from five agents to five hundred breaks ad-hoc patterns: conflicts over shared systems, duplicated work, no cost accountability, no way to know which agent did what. We build the orchestration layer that treats agents as a managed workforce — role definitions, task queues and bidding, shared-memory contracts, per-team budgets, kill switches, and a control tower showing fleet health, throughput and cost per completed task.

The orchestration core runs on durable execution (Temporal-class runtimes) with idempotent task semantics, priority lanes for SLA-bound work, and a policy engine that routes high-risk actions to approval workflows. Fleet upgrades are staged like software releases: shadow mode, canary cohorts, and automatic rollback on eval regression.
